title: The Collagen Protocol: What to Eat for Stronger Tendons
description:
Tendons are built from collagen, and collagen synthesis responds to what you eat and when you eat it. The gelatin and vitamin C protocol, explained with the study behind it.

Educational content, not medical advice.

#tendon #nutrition #collagen #calisthenics #fitness

scenes.caption: TENDONS ARE COLLAGEN
scenes.narration: Pinch the skin on the back of your hand. Pull it up. What you are holding is mostly collagen, the same protein your tendons are made of. Tendons are not muscle. They are rope, and rope is built from collagen fibres, laid down in the same direction, layer after layer. You do not build rope with protein shakes alone. You build it with the right raw material, at the right time.

scenes.label: OF YOUR BODY'S PROTEIN IS COLLAGEN
scenes.sub: the most common protein you own - and the one nobody feeds
scenes.narration: Thirty percent. That is roughly how much of all the protein in your body is collagen. It is the most common protein you own, it holds your tendons, your ligaments, your skin and your bones together, and almost nobody eats for it on purpose. The fitness world eats for muscle. Today, we eat for the cable.

scenes.head: STUDY - GELATIN + VITAMIN C
scenes.foot: Baar, 2017 - the study behind the protocol
scenes.narration: Here is the study. In 2017, researchers gave athletes fifteen grams of gelatin with vitamin C, one hour before training, and measured collagen synthesis in tendon tissue. It roughly doubled. Double. The timing matters because training increases blood flow to the tendon, and the building blocks arrive exactly when the tissue is asking for them.

scenes.title: THE PROTOCOL
layers: with it - fruit or a supplement
the rest of the day, every day
scenes.narration: So the protocol is simple. One hour before your tendon session, fifteen grams of gelatin or collagen with vitamin C. Then train. Then eat protein and sleep, because collagen is still built overnight, just like muscle. No magic powder, no secret food. Just the right material, delivered at the right hour.

scenes.caption: WHY TIMING WORKS
scenes.narration: Why does the timing work? Because a tendon at rest is almost closed off. It has very little blood flow, which is the same reason it heals slowly. But during training, blood flow to the tendon rises sharply, and for a few hours afterwards the tissue is open, hungry, and rebuilding. Gelatin taken an hour before lands in the bloodstream exactly as that window opens. Taken at a random hour, most of it goes everywhere else. Timing is not a detail here. Timing is the whole trick.

scenes.title: THE FULL DAY
scenes.narration: And the protocol does not end at the gym door. After training, eat a real meal with protein, because collagen synthesis needs amino acids all day, not just in one hour. Then sleep, because the deepest collagen building happens overnight, while you are still. Morning gelatin, afternoon training, evening meal, night sleep. That is the full day of feeding a tendon, and none of it costs more than a few coins.

scenes.caption: WHAT DOESN'T WORK
scenes.narration: And what does not work. A collagen drink taken once a week with no training. A protein shake after a workout that never loaded the tendon in the first place. Supplements bought by people who skip the session. The study did not test gelatin alone. It tested gelatin plus loading, at the right hour. Leave out either half and you are paying for expensive soup. The protocol is two halves, food and force, and they only work together.

scenes.caption: FEED IT, THEN LOAD IT
scenes.narration: One warning. Food does not replace training. Collagen without loading is just expensive soup. The protocol only works when the tendon is loaded the same hour, because loading is the signal that tells the body where to put the material. Feed it, then load it. Ninety days of both, and the spring gets stronger from the inside. Next video, we train tendons after forty, because the spring is not dead, it is just waiting. This is Wire Strength. Train the cable.
